citeAs: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen (2023). Evaluating Object Hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models. arXiv:2305.10355.
creator: Yifan Li, Yifan Du, Kun Zhou, Jinpeng Wang, Wayne Xin Zhao, Ji-Rong Wen (Renmin University of China, Meituan Group)
description: POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation) is a benchmark dataset for evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). It converts hallucination evaluation into a binary classification task by prompting LVLMs with simple Yes-or-No questions about objects in images (e.g., "Is there a car in the image?"). The dataset includes three evaluation settings — Random, Popular, and Adversarial — based on different negative object sampling strategies, built on top of MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, and GQA images.
name: POPE (Polling-based Object Probing Evaluation)
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: The paper validates POPE's stability by evaluating LLaVA with four different prompt templates and comparing the standard deviation of F1 scores (Avg±Std: 67.43±0.78) against CHAIR_I (13.88±3.22), showing POPE is significantly more stable. Consistency between POPE Yes/No responses and model-generated captions is also validated: out of 1303 and 1445 objects given "No" responses by InstructBLIP and MiniGPT-4, merely 0 and 5 appeared in captions respectively.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Each image is paired with polling questions constructed from a template "Is there a/an <object> in the image?". Ground-truth objects from annotations form "Yes" questions. Nonexistent objects are sampled under three strategies: (1) Random Sampling — randomly sample objects not in the image; (2) Popular Sampling — select the top-k most frequent objects in the dataset not present in the image; (3) Adversarial Sampling — rank objects by co-occurrence frequency with ground-truth objects and select top-k not present in the image. The ratio of ground-truth to nonexistent objects is set to 1:1 for label balance.
rai:dataBiases: The paper explicitly discusses that objects frequently appearing or co-occurring in visual instruction datasets (based on MSCOCO) are more likely to be hallucinated by LVLMs. The Popular and Adversarial sampling strategies in POPE are specifically designed to probe these biases. The unbalanced object distribution in MSCOCO (where top frequent objects occupy a major part) is acknowledged as a source of hallucination bias in LVLMs.
rai:dataCollection: POPE is constructed by sampling images from existing datasets (MSCOCO, A-OKVQA, GQA) and building polling questions from ground-truth object annotations or automatic segmentation results (SEEM). For MSCOCO, 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects are randomly selected from the validation set, and 6 questions are constructed per image (l=6). Ground-truth objects form "Yes" questions, while nonexistent objects are sampled under three strategies (Random, Popular, Adversarial) to form "No" questions, with a 1:1 ratio between positive and negative labels.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: The raw source data consists of images and object annotations from MSCOCO validation set, A-OKVQA, and GQA datasets. For MSCOCO, human-labeled object annotations covering 80 object categories from the MSCOCO segmentation challenge are used. Automatic segmentation annotations from SEEM (Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once) are also used for unannotated datasets.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator
rai:dataLimitations: The paper identifies several limitations: (1) POPE only focuses on coarse-grained object hallucination and does not cover fine-grained aspects such as object number, attributes, or positions. (2) Evaluation is conducted on a subset of the validation set, so results may be affected by data distribution. (3) POPE uses a matching-based method to determine Yes/No answers; LVLMs may occasionally fail to provide explicit Yes/No answers, leading to inaccurate evaluation. (4) When using automatic segmentation tools, object labels may be inconsistent with human annotations, causing divergence in results. (5) Only a small number of LVLMs were evaluated.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: For MSCOCO-based POPE, 500 images with more than 3 ground-truth objects are randomly selected from the validation set. Object annotations follow the 80 MSCOCO segmentation challenge categories. For scalability experiments, SEEM is used to automatically annotate images from A-OKVQA and GQA to extract object labels when human annotations are unavailable.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The paper discusses that object hallucination in LVLMs can hinder safe deployment in real-world applications. For example, an autonomous driving system with incorrect understanding of the external environment could make wrong decisions when encountering unexpected events, potentially leading to serious safety issues. The POPE benchmark aims to help identify and mitigate these hallucination issues to develop more reliable and human-aligned LVLMs.
rai:dataUseCases: POPE is intended for evaluating object hallucination in Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). It provides a stable, flexible, and scalable benchmark for measuring the degree to which LVLMs generate objects inconsistent with the target image. It can be extended to unannotated datasets using automatic segmentation tools, and can be used to compare hallucination levels across different LVLMs.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: SEEM (Segment Everything Everywhere All at Once) — an automatic segmentation tool used to annotate images from A-OKVQA and GQA datasets to extract ground-truth objects when human annotations are not available. ChatGPT is also used to assist in parsing open-ended VQA responses for evaluation.

null_reasons.rai:annotationsPerItem: The paper specifies 6 questions per image (l=6) but this refers to the number of polling questions, not independent annotations per item by multiple annotators.
null_reasons.rai:annotatorDemographics: POPE questions are constructed programmatically from existing annotations; no human annotators with demographics are described.
null_reasons.rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: No annotation platform (e.g., MTurk) is mentioned; questions are constructed automatically from existing dataset annotations.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionMissingData: No discussion of missing data handling in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataCollectionTimeframe: No specific data collection timeframe is mentioned in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataImputationProtocol: No imputation protocol is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:dataManipulationProtocol: No post-collection data manipulation (augmentation, resampling, etc.) is described for the POPE dataset itself.
null_reasons.rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: No versioning or maintenance plan is described in the paper.
null_reasons.rai:personalSensitiveInformation: The dataset consists of object-level image annotations with no personal or sensitive information collected.
null_reasons.license: No license is mentioned in the paper, and the HuggingFace dataset page for lmms-lab/POPE does not list a license.
